product_one_liner.value: Plannerly is a cloud-based BIM management platform that helps architecture, engineering and construction professionals plan, manage and verify BIM projects collaboratively.
product_one_liner.notes: Plannerly’s help article describes the cloud BIM management product, its planning/management/verification purpose, and the AEC project teams it serves.

pricing_page.notes: The public Plannerly pricing page lists Free, Pro and Company plans, so a public pricing page exists.

value: Queensland's Department of Transport and Main Roads
named_customers.notes: named_customers: Plannerly’s JTC case study names JTC and describes work moved into Plannerly; its Queensland case study explicitly says the Department of Transport and Main Roads uses Plannerly Verify. | named_customers.0: Plannerly’s case study identifies JTC and describes project work carried out in Plannerly. | named_customers.1: The case study explicitly names Queensland’s Department of Transport and Main Roads as a Plannerly Verify user.

employee_band.notes: The company overview reports 11–20 employees, matching the requested band.

hq_location.notes: hq_city: The LinkedIn company profile explicitly lists Plannerly’s headquarters as Irvine, California. | hq_country: The Plannerly company overview gives its location as Irvine, California, United States.

founded_year.notes: The LinkedIn company profile identifies Plannerly and states “Founded 2017.”

eng_blog.notes: The blog index identifies itself as a BIM/ISO 19650 guide blog and presents how-to and educational guide posts; it does not show an engineering or technical blog with posts about how the product is built.

public_docs.notes: The public Plannerly Help Center links to a collection with 68 articles, satisfying the requirement for several public documentation articles.

ai_ml_roles_open.notes: The Plannerly job-board company page reports zero jobs, so it shows no open AI/ML/data-science role.

model_provider.notes: Plannerly’s trust page names OpenAI in its explanation of AI features, identifying the publicly stated model provider.

compliance_certs.notes: The trust page attributes ISO 27001 certification and SOC 2 reports to infrastructure providers, while saying Plannerly’s own certification is still being prepared; it does not claim a completed company certification from the listed set.

last_funding.notes: funding_stage: The funding profile identifies the most recent listed round as an Accelerator round dated April 3, 2019. | funding_date: Caplight explicitly calls the Accelerator round on April 3, 2019 the company’s most recent round; this maps to 2019-04. The amount is not listed in the round record.

raised_18mo.notes: The source identifies April 3, 2019 as the most recent funding round, which predates the 18-month window ending November 9, 2026.

hiring_sdr_ae.notes: The Plannerly job-board company page reports zero jobs, so it shows no open SDR/BDR or account-executive role.

launched_6mo.notes: Plannerly published a product-features update dated October 15, 2026, inside the six-month window, describing newly updated BIM management software features.

leadership_change_12mo.notes: Louie Moran’s profile records a VP, Customer Success role at Plannerly ending in January 2026, within the 12 months before the stated run date.

crm_stack_signal.notes: crm_stack_signal: A case study states Plannerly uses Boundo to power its sales outbound motion, which is a directly identified sales system. | crm_stack_signal.0: The case study explicitly identifies Boundo as the system Plannerly uses for sales outbound.
